_comment: Cross-channel probe set for the knob2 v2 channel-axis A/B (docs/RECALL_SESSION_SCOPE_V2_DESIGN.md §5). Pairs with seed_corpus_v2.json. EVERY probe runs in channel cook-general (#料理) via per-query channel_id — the question the A/B answers is whether the maker-denshi (#電子工作) Raspberry-Pi-the-computer episodes contaminate a cooking conversation. `contaminant_keywords` for cooking probes are UNAMBIGUOUS electronics terms that only exist in the maker-denshi channel (GPIO / SDカード / はんだ / Raspberry Pi OS / ブレッドボード / I2C / 基板 / 回路 / 3Dプリンタ): if any appears + is elaborated, the model pulled a cross-channel episode = drift. NOTE the contaminant lists deliberately exclude the homophone ラズベリーパイ / ラズパイ itself, because in cook-general that word legitimately means the dessert — drift is measured only by the electronics-specific vocabulary that has no business in a baking chat. `false_positive: true` queries have no relevant memory in EITHER channel, so any memory_topic appearing is drift. Expected result: arm A (flag unset) leaks electronics terms into the magnet/meta cooking probes; arm B (CLOTO_RECALL_PERUSER_CHANNEL_AXIS=true) does not, because per-channel episode separation hides maker-denshi from cook-general — with no completion-rate (timeout) regression and no loss of cooking recall (arm B never removes cook-general's own episodes, only the other channel's). Japanese is intentional (JA-NLP fixture). Classifier is heuristic (README 'Classifier caveat') — good for relative A vs B, borderline cases want human/LLM-judge review.
